# MSc Health Analytics and Biostatistics Preparation Plan

## Phase 1: Biostatistics Foundations & Probability (Weeks 1 to 4)

### Week 1: Probability Distributions in Clinical Medicine
Core random variables, expectation, variance, binomial, and Poisson distributions in clinical contexts.
Estimated time: 120-180 min. Difficulty: 2. Verification: recall.

### Week 2: Statistical Inference & Hypothesis Testing
Null hypothesis testing, p-values, confidence intervals, type I and II errors, and power calculations.
Estimated time: 90-150 min. Difficulty: 2. Verification: applied.

### Week 3: Linear and Logistic Regression in Healthcare
Modeling continuous and binary health outcomes, odds ratios, and covariate adjustment.
Estimated time: 120-210 min. Difficulty: 2. Verification: applied.

### Week 4: Survival Analysis & Time-to-Event Data
Kaplan-Meier estimation, log-rank tests, and Cox proportional hazards models for clinical trials.
Estimated time: 120-240 min. Difficulty: 3. Verification: applied.

## Phase 2: Epidemiology & Clinical Study Design (Weeks 5 to 8)

### Week 5: Study Designs: Cohort, Case-Control & RCTs
Observational vs experimental designs, bias, confounding, and causal inference fundamentals.
Estimated time: 90-150 min. Difficulty: 2. Verification: recall.

### Week 6: Measures of Disease Occurrence & Risk
Incidence, prevalence, relative risk, attributable risk, and standardized rates.
Estimated time: 60-120 min. Difficulty: 1. Verification: recall.

### Week 7: Missing Data & Imputation in Health Studies
Mechanisms of missingness (MCAR, MAR, MNAR) and multiple imputation methods in clinical registries.
Estimated time: 90-180 min. Difficulty: 3. Verification: applied.

### Week 8: Meta-Analysis & Systematic Review Methods
Effect sizes, forest plots, heterogeneity (I-squared), and publication bias detection.
Estimated time: 90-180 min. Difficulty: 3. Verification: applied.

## Phase 3: Health Data Systems & Standards (Weeks 9 to 14)

### Week 9: Electronic Health Records & Clinical Coding
ICD-10, SNOMED-CT, LOINC, and RxNorm terminology mapping and ontologies.
Estimated time: 90-150 min. Difficulty: 2. Verification: recall.

### Week 10: Common Data Models: OMOP CDM & FHIR
Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) schema, HL7 FHIR resources, and interoperability.
Estimated time: 120-240 min. Difficulty: 3. Verification: applied.

### Week 11: Clinical Data Extraction & SQL Cohort Building
Extracting patient cohorts, index dates, observational windows, and adverse event flags from relational EHR.
Estimated time: 120-210 min. Difficulty: 2. Verification: applied.

### Week 12: Phenotyping Algorithms & Validation
Rule-based and probabilistic clinical phenotyping for identifying disease cohorts.
Estimated time: 90-180 min. Difficulty: 3. Verification: applied.

## Phase 4: Machine Learning in Health Analytics (Weeks 15 to 20)

### Week 13: Clinical Risk Prediction Models
Developing, validating, and reporting multivariable prediction models using TRIPOD guidelines.
Estimated time: 120-240 min. Difficulty: 3. Verification: applied.

### Week 14: Discrimination, Calibration & Clinical Utility
C-statistic / AUROC, Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
Estimated time: 90-180 min. Difficulty: 3. Verification: applied.

### Week 15: Ethics, Fairness & Privacy in Healthcare AI
Algorithmic bias across demographics, differential privacy, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance.
Estimated time: 60-120 min. Difficulty: 2. Verification: recall.

### Week 16: Applied Capstone: Reproducible Health Analytics Study
End-to-end cohort selection, statistical modeling, validation, and reproducible report generation.
Estimated time: 180-360 min. Difficulty: 4. Verification: artifact.
